objective: Compile a portable Academy skill that chooses and proves the smallest justified human-agent execution graph with typed authority, state, recovery, termination, and budget boundaries.

deliverables.description: An Agent Skills-compatible execution graph engineering package with explicit system-shape and proof gates.

context.audience: AI architects, workflow engineers, academy operators, institutions, and human-agent system builders

stakes.rationale: Incorrect execution topology can widen authority, leak data, waste spend, or lose work, but a draft graph can be rejected before activation.

must: Compare the proposed graph against a deterministic workflow, one loop, and sequential skill composition.
Attenuate authority across every edge and terminate every cycle.
Define idempotency, recovery, escalation, wall-time, parallelism, and spend before activation.
mustNot: Create graph structure merely to increase agent count or visual complexity.
Persist chain-of-thought or undeclared private learner state as graph state.
Grant money, publication, credential, external-message, destructive, or permission-expansion authority to an agent.

completionTests.value: Bind each node to the least-powerful viable executor
